desc:
A derangement of 1..n is an ordering p of the numbers 1..n in which no number sits at its own place: p[i] != i + 1 for every index i (0-indexed). In other words, the number 1 may not be first, 2 may not be second, and so on.

Return every derangement as a row. Rows may be returned in any order. If there is none, return an empty list.

n = 3  ->  [[2,3,1], [3,1,2]]
n = 2  ->  [[2,1]]
n = 1  ->  []
constraints: There are at most 1,854 derangements for these values of n
hints: Build the ordering from the left, one slot at a time, and keep track of which numbers are already used.
Slot i (0-indexed) may take any unused number except i + 1.
Recurse slot by slot. When all n slots are filled, copy the current row into the answer. Undo your choice (mark the number unused again) before trying the next number.
editorial: This is the standard permutation search with one extra rule. Keep a used flag per number and the current row. At slot i try every number v from 1 to n that is unused and different from i + 1; place it, recurse to slot i + 1, then remove it. When the row is full it is a derangement, so store a copy.

Because the rule is checked while the row is built, branches that already break it are never extended. The number of rows is the derangement number D(n) = 1, 0, 1, 2, 9, 44, 265, 1854 for n = 0..7, so the work is roughly proportional to the output size times n.
solution:
def listDerangements(n):
    res = []
    cur = []
    used = [False] * (n + 1)

    def go(i):
        if i == n:
            res.append(cur[:])
            return
        for v in range(1, n + 1):
            if used[v] or v == i + 1:
                continue
            used[v] = True
            cur.append(v)
            go(i + 1)
            cur.pop()
            used[v] = False

    go(0)
    return res
